title: Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District pits longtime incumbent Democrat Rosa DeLauro, who has held the seat since 1991, against Republican challenger Christopher Lancia, a Coast Guard veteran and federal law enforcement officer. DeLauro won the Democratic convention nomination with 87% of delegate votes after primary challengers Andrew Rice and Damjan DeNoble failed to qualify for the ballot; Rice is considering an independent run. The district, which includes New Haven and surrounding areas, is strongly Democratic and has not elected a Republican since the 1980s. The primary election is scheduled for August 11, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for this race were found as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Rosa DeLauro
candidates.summary: Rosa DeLauro is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 1990. She serves as the Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee and is known for her progressive advocacy on issues including child tax credits, food safety, workers' rights, and healthcare. She has won re-election by large margins in every election since taking office.

candidates.name: Christopher Lancia
candidates.summary: Christopher Lancia is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District. He served in the U.S. Coast Guard and later as a federal law enforcement officer. Lancia has been active in Connecticut Republican Party politics, previously managing a congressional campaign and seeking the state party chairmanship. He is running on a platform focused on affordability, energy costs, veterans' services, tax cuts, and reduced government spending.
